notes: Source: v0.1.83 commit c8de589e74464c67ba42e42c90f7d169ef205a45. This mapping covers every top-level property in the original create<AppState> factory exactly once; it does not classify module-scope exports/helpers, which must also move separately.

Keep one physical Zustand store and the existing flat public state/action API. State ownership does not require cross-domain commands to call several setters: preserve every original action function body, each existing single-set transaction, and original side-effect order during extraction.

appStore.ts is the compatibility facade only. No slice, command, runtime, pure reducer, or pure selector may import appStore.ts or the instantiated root store. Supply get/set/store/API via an injected context; use import type for shared state/contracts.

activeContext owns activeTaskId/homeSpaceId/draft and active model/permission/connector/mode values together. models/defaultModelId/modelPreferences belong to appConfig. activeProjectId and activeWorkspaceId are navigation state, not chat-context identity.

Task.messages remains the canonical renderer conversation array inside Task. pendingRegenerations and compactionByTask are task-keyed state. Pure applyPatchToMessage and history/text helpers must be shared with btwStore independently of either singleton.

Project navigation preserves requestProjectNav/projectNavRequest/applyProjectNavigation and its external dirty-form guard. Do not immediately overwrite activeProjectId when the original action queues a request. TaskDraft.projectId and Task.projectId stay in their existing structures, not duplicated in projectsSlice.

capabilities contains only installed/market skills, experts, and connectors plus their catalog-management actions. Expert summons/bindings/switching, external-agent pinning, and active connector selection belong to task commands, not capability catalogs.

initRuntime is assigned whole for mechanical extraction; subsequently decompose bootstrap/subscriptions/event routing inside runtime without changing event order, API call semantics, or Pi 1.3.0 integration. No fallback copy of the old appStore implementation should remain.

Move module-scope unsubs, pendingPinTaskIds, pendingMoveSpaceIds, pendingMoveTaskIds, deletedTaskRuntimeTombstones, pendingTaskMetadataHydrations, externalHistoryHydrations, moveChain, renderHydration, and related mutable runtime values into one per-store runtime context. Share the same moveChain between both workspace move commands and the same tombstones between deletion/restoration and event projection.

runtime/artifactProjection owns the event/snapshot reducer wrappers and message-artifact reconciliation. artifactProjection is discardable main-domain projection; artifactPolicies is display-only filtering; caches are rendering data. Do not recreate task.artifacts or turn a render cache into domain truth.

runtime/artifactRender should co-locate the existing render-hydrator closure/helper with its ensureArtifactRenderPayload action rather than leave an otherwise orphan one-line wrapper. Cache and descriptor access must use injected get/set, not facade imports.

commands/workspaceMoves keeps bindTaskSpace, moveSpace, and moveTaskInWorkspaceTree together; preserve common serialization, per-id pending guards, source/target archive checks, affected-sibling rollback, homeSpace synchronization, and unrelated concurrent message updates.

commands/taskDraft preserves the distinct original reset behavior of startProjectTask/newTask/summonExpert. Drafts remain unmaterialized until first send; do not merge reset algorithms as a refactor convenience.

Maintain active-task guards for task-specific async UI hydration, ordered batched agent deltas and unchanged references, regeneration two-phase commit, delete tombstones, Project Plan linking after first persisted send, and terminal owner/sessionId isolation. PTY data continues to bypass Zustand.

All action groups have fewer than 600 original source lines before imports/types; the largest is commands/workspaceMoves. The module count is a responsibility map, not a requirement to split each action into a file. Small slice files own their defaults and narrow state operations.
